nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. If $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$, written in lowest terms as $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ with $b, d > 0$, then $bc = ad + 1$.
nodes.title: Consecutive Farey fractions have determinant one

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ be elements of the Farey set $F_n$, written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$. If $bc = ad + 1$ and $n < b + d$, then $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$.
nodes.title: Determinant one and large denominator sum give Farey neighbors

nodes.summary: If $m \le n$ are natural numbers, then every element of the Farey set $F_m$ belongs to $F_n$, that is, $F_m \subseteq F_n$.
nodes.title: Farey sets grow with the order

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Farey set $F_n$ of order $n$ is the finite set of rationals $a/d$ with $a$ and $d$ natural numbers, $1 \le d \le n$ and $0 \le a \le d$.
nodes.title: Farey set

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Farey sequence of order $n$ is the list of the elements of the Farey set $F_n$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: Farey sequence

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. A rational number $q$ belongs to the Farey set $F_{n+1}$ if and only if $q$ belongs to $F_n$, or there are Farey neighbors $x$ and $y$ of order $n$ whose denominators in lowest terms sum to $n + 1$ such that $q$ is the mediant of $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Mediants generate the next Farey set

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ be elements of the Farey set $F_n$, written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$. Then $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$ if and only if $bc = ad + 1$ and $n < b + d$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic characterization of Farey neighbors

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, rationals $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$ when both lie in the Farey set $F_n$, $x < y$, and no element $z$ of $F_n$ satisfies $x < z < y$.
nodes.title: Farey neighbors

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $x$ and $y$ be Farey neighbors of order $n$ whose denominators in lowest terms sum to $n + 1$. Then the mediant of $x$ and $y$ belongs to the Farey set $F_{n+1}$ and does not belong to $F_n$.
nodes.title: Mediants that enter the next Farey set

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. If $x$ and $y$ are Farey neighbors of order $n$, then the mediant of $x$ and $y$ does not belong to the Farey set $F_n$.
nodes.title: The mediant of Farey neighbors is not in the Farey set

nodes.summary: For rational numbers $x = a/b$ and $y = c/d$ written in lowest terms with $b, d > 0$, the mediant of $x$ and $y$ is the rational number $(a + c)/(b + d)$.
nodes.title: Mediant

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a rational number $q$, $q$ belongs to the Farey set $F_n$ of order $n$ if and only if $0 \le q \le 1$ and the denominator of $q$ in lowest terms is at most $n$.
nodes.title: Membership in the Farey set

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F_n$ be the Farey set of order $n$. If $x < y$ are neighbors in $F_n$, meaning that $x, y \in F_n$ and no element of $F_n$ lies strictly between them, then the denominators $b$ of $x$ and $d$ of $y$ in lowest terms satisfy $b + d > n$.
nodes.title: Farey neighbors have denominator sum exceeding the order

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
